mechanisms.name: `rotationPolicy` default changes from `Never` to `Always` (breaking, on by default)
resourcesConsumers: mesh-root-ca Certificate (not affected, because of an explicit setting)
mechanisms.mechanism: Neither leaf Certificate sets privateKey.rotationPolicy, so from 1.18 each renewal (roughly every 20 days, 720h - 240h) generates a new key. The first renewal after the upgrade is the first rotation; no re-issuance is forced at upgrade time. nginx loads tls.crt/tls.key once at start or reload and nothing in the repo reloads it. That problem already exists today: a renewed cert does not reach a running nginx, so ledger's served cert would expire after 30 days. Rotation adds a second risk: Kubernetes swaps the Secret volume atomically, but nginx opens the two files separately, so a reload or worker start that straddles a swap can read a mismatched cert/key pair. With a constant key this race was harmless; with a rotating key it produces a mismatch error. checkout re-reads the files on every call and has the same small race. The assessment calls this a latent hazard, not an immediate failure. If the root's key were rotated, mutual TLS would break until both Secrets and both workloads were refreshed, which would be an outage of the payments mesh.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: mesh-root-ca is not affected because env/platform/pki/overlays/prod/mesh-root-ca-prod.yaml sets `rotationPolicy: Never` and clusters/prod/pki.yaml deploys the prod overlay. This is not confirmed in built output. For the leaves there is no mitigation in the repo; the assessment recommends setting the policy explicitly and verifying ledger's reload behaviour.
assumptions: Strategic-merge patches normally merge `privateKey` and keep `algorithm` and `size` (must be confirmed)
Root renewal at 1 year, 720h before expiry
missingEvidence: No built Kustomize manifest for the pki overlay; `rendered/` contains only the Helm output, so the rendered mesh-root-ca rotationPolicy: Never is not confirmed
ledger's nginx reload behaviour is not visible (no reloader sidecar, no Reloader/stakater annotation, no shareProcessNamespace, no checksum annotation)
Live notAfter dates and renewal timing, which determine when the first rotation happens
Whether Certificates outside the repo lack an explicit rotationPolicy
recommendedValidation: `kustomize build env/platform/pki/overlays/prod` and `.../apps/payments/overlays/prod`; confirm mesh-root-ca has privateKey.rotationPolicy: Never with algorithm ECDSA and size 256 preserved, and that the leaves have no rotationPolicy

Set rotationPolicy explicitly (Always or Never) on ledger-tls and checkout-tls in a commit before the upgrade; do not rely on the gate `DefaultPrivateKeyRotationPolicyAlways: false`, because 1.19 removes it

In staging, upgrade and run `cmctl renew -n payments ledger-tls checkout-tls`; verify tls.key changes, checkout still reaches ledger, ledger serves the new cert (openssl s_client), and no key/cert mismatch is logged; add a reload mechanism if needed before the first prod renewal
Compare the mesh-root-ca Secret tls.key fingerprint and ca.crt before and after the upgrade; both must be unchanged and the Certificate must show no new revision

mechanisms.name: Rendered chart changes with a rollout footprint (not in the release-notes breaking list)
resourcesConsumers: CRDs (signatureAlgorithm, profile, Vault serverName, iss/ciss shortNames)
Argo CD sync ordering (cert-manager wave 0, pki wave 1, payments wave 2)
anyone who has bound to or audited the old role name
mechanisms.mechanism: The challenges ClusterRole/Binding is replaced. With Argo prune: true there is a short rollout window in which old and new bindings differ. This affects only ACME challenges, which are unused here, so there is no functional impact, but it matters for external references to the old role name. The webhook probes change from port 6080 to the named port `healthcheck`. New additive CRD content includes the iss/ciss shortNames, which could conflict. The CRD update rides on this Argo sync. The webhook validates and mutates every cert-manager resource, so pki (wave 1) must not apply while the new webhook is not yet ready.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: ACME is unused, so the RBAC change has no functional impact. The probe change is consistent because the container defines name: healthcheck on 6080 (verified in the render). The CRD additions are additive. ServerSideApply=true avoids the annotation-size limit on the large CRDs.
citedEvidence: `rendered/to.yaml:12355-12356` (container defines name: healthcheck on 6080; verified in the render)
missingEvidence: Argo CD application health under the pruned and replaced RBAC objects, and the webhook-readiness ordering, were not testable from files alone
External references to the old role name
Conflicts of iss/ciss with other CRDs or with scripts/aliases on the cluster
recommendedValidation: Run the upgrade through Argo with the webhook and startupapicheck observed: the cert-manager Application becomes Healthy, the CRDs update, the old challenges ClusterRole is pruned without error, and pki and payments then sync
Search for external references to `cert-manager-controller-challenges` (RBAC audits, policy-as-code) and for conflicts with the `iss` and `ciss` shortNames
Plan the rollback: check that reverting to 1.17.2 does not strand any field (CRDs keep: true); do not use signatureAlgorithm or profile until the upgrade is settled

mechanisms.name: Security advisory GHSA-8rvj-mm4h-c258: "Direct ACME Challenge resources can bypass Issuer DNS01 solver policy"
resourcesConsumers: ClusterIssuers with a DNS01 solver (none here)
mechanisms.mechanism: The advisory is rated high and affects >= 1.18.0, <= 1.20.2, with fixes only in 1.19.6 and 1.20.3. There is no 1.18.x fix, so upgrading to any 1.18 puts the cluster inside the affected range; 1.17.2 is outside it.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: Exploitability here is very low. It needs a ClusterIssuer with a DNS01 solver, and there are none; there is only a CA issuer and a SelfSigned issuer. It is, however, a reason to treat 1.18 as a stepping stone to 1.19.6+.
citedEvidence: GHSA-8rvj-mm4h-c258 (the copy in `upstream/` is an HTML capture of the advisory page)
missingEvidence: Only the advisory's metadata and summary were read; versions not verified beyond what it states
recommendedValidation: Schedule the follow-up to 1.19.6+/1.20.3+ because of the GHSA
